baer-heitev/2:ד: (4) When there is possibility [to do both]. But if he is close to nightfall he reads the Megillah, for a dead mitzvah can possibly be buried at night; but if it is a situation where it is impossible to bury him afterward because of bandits, certainly Megillah reading is postponed — see Magen Avraham and Taz. Milah and Megillah reading — if there is time for both, Megillah reading comes first because of publicizing the miracle (Pri Chadash). But in Terumat HaDeshen siman 262 [263] he sided to say the opposite — when there is time, milah comes first, and when there is no time, Megillah reading comes first. And it appears to me the reason is that he can circumcise on the ninth [if the eighth was Shabbat]. Knesset HaGedolah — see there.
beur-hagra/2:ד: (4) And all this etc. — so too is the law there that nevertheless they cancel their work etc., meaning they can complete afterward the work since it is d'oraisa; and his words are puzzling — for if so, that which Rava asks there about Megillah reading and nevertheless etc., meaning since both postpone work and Torah study, and if so, in any case nevertheless it is preferable that work is completely postponed; and in Sanhedrin 35a "nevertheless burial nevertheless postpones Shabbat" etc., and so for other mitzvot as I wrote regarding milah etc., and he listed these even though they have karet, and all the more so for the rest, and the same for Megillah.
beur-hagra/2:ה: (ה) But if so — for one answer: Tosafot Pesachim ch. 10 and Nazir ch. 1 that Kiddush on wine is d'oraisa, and Shabbat 77b defers it — not as written here; Ran holds another version and Rambam as cited, and from the language to sanctify on wine etc.
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: b) There. A person is obligated to read the Megillah at night etc., and know that the essence of Megillah reading is by day, as Tosafot daf 4 wrote and so too R' Meir in his rulings. And he wrote in responsa Noda B'Yehuda Orach Chayyim siman 41 that night reading is d'rabbanan and day reading is divrei kabbalah — see there. From Mechaber letter 1 regarding time.
levushei-serad/2:_: Taz seif 2 — surely it is void to say so etc. The difficulty is: that which is void means surely for sake of human dignity, and if so it is an argument on the derashah, and the body of the pilpul is whether human dignity postpones Megillah — indeed it is simple that initially Taz speaks when it is possible to bury afterward, and he holds like Magen Avraham seif 6 that delay of burial more than the state's law is nullification of human dignity; and since the gemara stated the reason is because of the great [principle of] human dignity, we learn it is completely postponed (and what one can question on this proof — there regarding "and you shall not ignore" is as if no time — see what I wrote in the discourse just before to explain Magen Avraham's first proof; this is understood also from Taz's proof, and delve). And afterward he added to bring proof from no time, meaning the dogs will eat him — this is certainly void; if so, it also implies that even when there is time the law is so, since advancing burial by state law is called human dignity. And it is clear.
magen-avraham/2:ב: (2) that you have no [one greater than you] etc. — it implies he holds that even public Torah study they cancel; but in the gemara it implies they do not cancel public [study] [so it is], and see Radbaz 13 [siman 137], and Bach wrote public Torah study means of all Israel, and so too in Tosafos s.v. nevertheless preferable etc. see there; and nevertheless it appears to me that in any case they must read Megillah; however an individual must cancel his study and go to read in congregation, but plural does not apply — that even if each individual learns by himself it is called plural since each cancels, and so too in Tosafos.
magen-avraham/2:ג: (3) as needed. — it implies he holds that even if he has gravediggers, since they are not as needed, it is called a dead mitzvah [corpse without attendants]; and so in Hagahot end siman 296 he holds burial of one's dead takes precedence; and it requires study, for we say plainly to me: Megillah and Temple service — Megillah is preferable; dead mitzvah and Temple service — dead mitzvah is preferable; dead mitzvah and Megillah — what? etc., and resolve: that which we say dead mitzvah is preferable to Temple service is specifically for a corpse that has no gravediggers, but burial of relatives does not postpone Temple service, and so in Tosafos Shevuos 30b; and if so, plainly Megillah is preferable to burial of relatives, for Megillah is preferable even to Temple service; however this can be deflected, but truth guides its way as Ramban wrote in Sha'ar HaGemul that dead mitzvah he speaks specifically; rather the opening that says nevertheless preferable is Torah study speaks of all dead; see there. And so Tosafos, and see siman 526 in name of Shelah; and so Semag — specifically when he is in the field that he lies in disgrace, but in the city Megillah first, and so Bach, and so in Darkei Moshe in name of Or Zarua who wrote burial of a Torah scholar precedes Megillah — end; and his reason is from what we say honor of Torah of an individual is stricter — it implies for any other person Megillah precedes, and so is primary, and so in Berachos 20a burial of relatives is not called human dignity since he lies in the city, and if so it does not postpone Megillah, and so in Ra'avad siman 62.
mishnah-berurah/1:א: (1) To read Megillah at night — from the time stars emerge, and see below siman 692 seif 4 in Mishna Berurah and Biur Halacha what we wrote there.
mishnah-berurah/2:ה: (11) There is no d'oraisa mitzvah that is postponed etc. — because Megillah reading is only d'rabbanan, and see Taz who brought in name of Rashal and Bach that always Megillah reading precedes because of publicizing the miracle, and the Gra in his Biur also holds so — see there.
peri-megadim/1:א: (א) And to repeat it — Taz: Rashi Megillah 8a, Gemara derives from the verse "I will read by day" etc. and "by night" etc.; for Rashi's reason, if he erred and did not read at daybreak — there is remembrance of the miracle when they cried while people were still sleeping at dawn and by day at sunrise.
peri-megadim/1:ג: (3) I will further explain to you that Beit Yosef here and Shulchan Aruch brings in siman 693 divides minchah — one may be lenient for forced persons; and in Pri Chadash there he questioned him that it is not like Shema, and see what Magen Avraham wrote from this. And apparently in any case between sunset, whenever there is force one may read — a rabbinic doubt we rule leniently (siman 89 regarding stringency l'chatchila one does not do a rabbinic doubt — Magen Avraham 6 and Taz 5); not so when there is force and twilight, for this principle was not said to include Megillah, for which twilight b'dieved etc.; and per what Taz wrote divrei kabbalah, one can say at twilight he does not fulfill also from Shema — difficult, say to include Shema. Taz here 2. And with God's help in siman 479 seif 2 I will explain further.
peri-megadim/2:_: Outside — Taz: what Rashi wrote, see Maharsha there; and Taz holds per the conclusion in Berachos 20b responsa that it does not postpone even a Torah prohibition — see what we wrote in our novellae Berachos and Megillah. And what Rambam wrote in this language means the Mechaber's language was copied from there. And what is in the intention of the late R' Moshe — one can say why did the late R' Moshe not write a greater novelty that Megillah is completely postponed because of a dead mitzvah (Magen Avraham letter 6); and what Rama's words contradict each other — apparently one can say when there is no time to do both, surely no d'oraisa mitzvah is postponed because of Megillah reading, not so a dead mitzvah when there is time to bury afterward and for Megillah there is no time — therefore Megillah precedes; but if impossible to bury afterward, dead mitzvah precedes; and his view that in this moment he delays the corpse is considered complete nullification of a mitzvah — nevertheless this is not a contradiction; and in Sha'ar HaTziyun in the section on human dignity we extended; and what he wrote a fortiori that Temple service should be completely postponed because of Megillah reading — Torah study is preferable to Temple service and is completely set aside in this moment because of Megillah reading — his intent is public Torah study is preferable to Temple service and nevertheless is postponed because of Megillah reading as the Mechaber wrote you have no one greater etc. (Magen Avraham 3), and nevertheless is completely postponed — all the more Temple service which is completely postponed because of Megillah which is divrei kabbalah and weighed like d'oraisa — publicizing the miracle is preferable. It appears specifically when impossible to read Megillah afterward; but when possible to read afterward, a passing d'oraisa mitzvah a standing d'oraisa mitzvah is preferable — and see siman 684 to precede etc. And the authority of Rabbeinu that they cancel Torah study to hear Megillah in congregation — still requires study. And that we pray and recite Shema and afterward Megillah that they read in congregation as Magen Avraham letter 3 wrote — in congregation there is no negligence in congregation, and this is simple. And what Taz wrote in siman 478 that bread on Shabbat before havdalah d'oraisa precedes — see there in Pri Megadim; not so here Megillah is kabbalah and weighed like d'oraisa and publicizing the miracle is preferable — and that he concluded here publicizing etc. And there we wrote if bread is d'oraisa see there; however the authority of Rabbeinu — a fortiori from Temple service — Taz should have proved plainly that Torah study is completely nullified completely at this hour and Temple service can be done afterward, and there is no a fortiori — we learn Temple service is completely nullified because of Megillah when there is no time for both. And what Tosafos Megillah 3a s.v. they cancel — in our novellae we wrote from this.
turei-zahav/2:א: (1) Except for a dead mitzvah etc. In Rambam it is written in this language that whoever encounters him buries him first and afterward reads. And Mizrachi was precise that "and afterward he reads" is superfluous language, rather it teaches us: if there is time to read afterward — yes; if not — no. And it requires study, for plainly in the gemara dead mitzvah is preferable to Megillah, for the master said: great is human dignity that postpones a Torah prohibition, and the postponement is that the negative commandment is completely set aside, meaning as Rashi explained that it is written "you cannot ignore" and it is written "and you ignored" — times that you ignore, such as an elder not according to his honor; if so, in Megillah reading too human dignity should completely postpone the Megillah, and it is a fortiori, for Megillah is only from rabbinic enactment; and the extra language Mizrachi was precise on does not appear to come on that intent, rather per what Tosafos wrote "and you asked — let them do their service immediately and afterward read Megillah alone," and one can say it is better to read with the congregation because there is greater publicizing of the miracle — end; and for that intent Rambam wrote nevertheless: whoever has both before him and both have ample time — a Torah prohibition, because of publicizing the miracle in congregation, Megillah precedes — it teaches us that in this we are not concerned for greater publicity, rather he reads it individually afterward; but if there are no hours afterward, Rambam is not dealing with this, and the law is they completely cancel Megillah because human dignity postpones it; and know this: would one who finds a dead mitzvah in a field without a Megillah with him throw away the corpse and go to the city to read Megillah, and perhaps thereby dogs will eat it — and is it said he should do so? Surely it is void to say so; and apart from this there is no substance to Shulchan Aruch here whose words contradict each other — at first Rama wrote but if it is impossible to do both etc., implying other mitzvot precede Megillah; and at end wrote specifically when possible to read afterward, implying when impossible to read afterward Megillah precedes nevertheless, all the more other mitzvot. Regarding Megillah and Temple service that we say in gemara Megillah is preferable and we derive it from what is written family and family to bring priestly families and Levitical families who cancel their service and come to hear Megillah reading — Ran wrote; however specifically when they can afterward complete the service — if not so, surely they do not cancel d'oraisa service because of d'rabbanan Megillah; and it requires study on this, for we say Megillah is preferable to Torah study, and there Torah study is completely postponed because of it — meaning the study he has now an obligation in this hour cannot be made up in compensation, for what he will learn later is a mitzvah in itself, and nevertheless it is postponed because of Megillah — the same also for service; and it is a fortiori, for we say in gemara Torah study is preferable to service. Also Rambam's language he copied here instructs so, that he wrote a fortiori for other mitzvot that all are postponed because of it, and including this surely they too are completely postponed; and this is certain that you will find mitzvot dependent on that time, and nevertheless when they are postponed they are completely postponed; and what Ran wrote that service is d'oraisa and Megillah d'rabbanan — one can say it is divrei kabbalah, for we rule divrei kabbalah like d'oraisa as Beit Yosef wrote siman 554 in name of Rabbenu Tam regarding tzitzit; and therefore we properly say service is postponed; and Beit Yosef wrote Tosafos's view is like Ran who wrote: priests cancel their service to hear Megillah, and one asks why they cancel — is there not much time for service after the reading? And one can say since day has brightened it is time for service and they set it aside for the reading, it is called cancellation — end; and I do not see proof from this to agree with Ran — Tosafos refers to Talmud language who said they cancel their service, meaning at the time of their service every day when day has brightened, and on this they challenge "but there is time afterward all day"; but if it happens service was not done until a little before its time ends and Megillah reading is before him — so too Megillah completely postpones service since impossible to fulfill both — publicizing the miracle is preferable, as appeared to me.
yad-ephraim/1:_: In Magen Avraham beginning siman he wrote in Hagahot Minhagim etc., and it appears to me he does not read etc. — see below siman 688 Taz seif 2, or what he wrote, and possibly in time of pressure the measure is until sunrise, and what Magen Avraham wrote implies that after they did not read etc. — I did not know what difference between a convert who converted after [dawn] and it appears also for Hagahot Maimoniot he need not read after dawn since his mitzvah essence is by day, and the convert cited is because among Israel it is not common to sin [regarding Megillah at night].
